tldr: Application Gateway for Containers is previewing MCP routing, JWT validation and private frontends—new options for securing and publishing AI services on Azure.
Azure SQL can now keep point-in-time recovery backups immutable for the configured retention period, beyond the previous seven-day default.
Data-center power delays are pushing some builders toward repurposed jet engines, a reminder that grid access can constrain AI capacity as much as GPUs.

top.title: Application Gateway for Containers adds MCP server routing
top.summary: A new MCPRoute custom resource lets teams publish MCP servers behind a stable hostname and path, with centralized TLS, JWT validation and Web Application Firewall controls.
top.why: Evaluate it if you need to expose MCP servers: it could centralize ingress and security policy instead of leaving each server to handle those controls.

top.title: Application Gateway for Containers previews centralized JWT validation
top.summary: The AuthPolicy resource can validate JWT signatures, issuer, lifetime and configured audience using signing keys retrieved from a trusted source.
top.why: For services behind this gateway, assess whether you can move token checks out of individual workloads and manage them consistently at ingress.

top.title: Application Gateway for Containers previews private frontends
top.summary: Private frontends can be reached only through approved Azure Private Link private endpoints, keeping internal applications and cross-cluster traffic off public ingress.
top.why: Check this option when designing internal AI or shared services that must remain private, as it may simplify how you expose them across networks.

top.title: Site Recovery improves disaster recovery for VMSS Flex
top.summary: Azure Site Recovery is generally available with improved target configuration and end-to-end recovery workflows, including failover and reprotection, for VMs in flexible-orchestration scale sets.
top.why: Revisit recovery plans for VMSS Flex workloads: the improved workflow may make this configuration practical to protect with Site Recovery.

top.title: Azure SQL can keep PITR backups immutable for the full retention period
top.summary: A preview lets you lock point-in-time recovery backup retention against changes for the configured retention period, beyond the existing seven days of immutable backups; the update cites 35-day retention as a typical financial-sector need.
top.why: If your recovery or compliance policy requires tamper-resistant backups beyond a week, check whether this preview can meet that requirement.

also.title: Azure Files previews expanded data protection and recovery
also.summary: The preview adds business-continuity capabilities for recovering Azure Files data after accidental changes, regional disruption or ransomware, within or across regions.

also.title: Azure Storage Discovery previews richer capacity insights
also.summary: The preview adds storage-usage views including access patterns, data age, storage tiers, object-size distribution and retention.

also.title: Azure Databricks article examines overlapping workspace CIDRs
also.summary: The networking post considers whether three workspaces using the same VNet address range require renumbering, or whether user access patterns offer another way to address the conflict.

top.title: Grid delays push data centers toward repurposed jet engines
top.summary: With grid connections and new turbines taking years, some data-center builders are turning to discarded jet engines for power, despite their lower efficiency and greater environmental impact.
top.why: Include grid connection and interim power availability in capacity plans; GPU procurement alone will not determine when a site can serve workloads.

top.title: AMD reports nearly doubled data-center sales as AI demand grows
top.summary: AMD said its third-quarter data-center sales almost doubled year over year, helping it beat expectations as demand for AI infrastructure grew.
top.why: Keep accelerator sourcing assumptions under review and compare viable hardware options rather than basing capacity plans on a single vendor.

top.title: CrowdStrike to acquire two AI security startups
top.summary: CrowdStrike disclosed plans to acquire AI security companies Fiddler AI and Dreadnode; the Wall Street Journal reported a combined price of $495 million.
top.why: Track how security vendors fold agent and AI protections into existing platforms before deciding whether to build or buy those controls.

also.title: Report says Anthropic's compute margins are worsening
also.summary: The report says Anthropic's compute margins are getting worse even though they might be expected to improve, highlighting the continuing cost pressure of running its models.

top.title: Developer says Postman installed plugins in coding agents without consent
top.summary: A developer alleges Postman's desktop app installed plugins into Claude Code and OpenAI Codex without permission, changing the agents' environments.
top.why: Review desktop-app permissions and agent plugin policies in managed developer environments; treat integrations that can modify coding agents as part of your software supply chain.
